title: Phase 4.5-4.6: Verify TOCTOU mitigations and full pipeline
description:
Verify TOCTOU analysis and end-to-end pipeline.

## 4.5 TOCTOU mitigations:
- [ ] pidfd_open() immediately after SO_PEERCRED verification (Linux 5.3+)
- [ ] memfd_create for secret injection (no filesystem path to race)
- [ ] Fallback for older kernels: /proc/<pid>/exe symlink verification
- [ ] macOS: LOCAL_PEERPID + session token authentication
- [ ] PreToolUse hook → command execution: NOT VULNERABLE (check IS execution path)
- [ ] Bwrap sandbox setup: NOT VULNERABLE (clone() with namespace flags is atomic)

## 4.6 Full execution pipeline:
- [ ] Wire everything together: parse → resolve → sandbox → execute → scrub → return
- [ ] Error handling:
  - If sigild unreachable: fail loudly with clear error (no silent passthrough)
  - If placeholder cannot resolve: fail with error listing missing path
  - If sandbox creation fails: fall back to hook-only mode with warning

## Red team tests:
- From inside sandbox: attempt ptrace (should fail via seccomp)
- From inside sandbox: attempt /proc/<sigild_pid>/mem (should fail via PID namespace)
- From inside sandbox: modify PATH or LD_PRELOAD (should be blocked)
- Verify sandbox overhead < 30ms with cached secrets
- Test with real Claude Code Bash tool calls end-to-end

## Acceptance
- All TOCTOU surfaces have mitigations
- Full pipeline works end-to-end
- Sandbox overhead is < 30ms

All TOCTOU mitigations verified and documented. Fixed 2 failing tests by:

description:
Evidence: CHANGELOG.md has a [0.5.0] - 2026-07-07 section, workspace.package version in Cargo.toml is 0.5.0, and bead bf-rnh9 ("Cut v0.5.0 release") was closed with acceptance criteria "GitHub release v0.5.0 exists with sigil and sigild assets". Root cause found on iad-ci cluster: `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig get workflows -n argo-workflows | grep sigil-ci` shows 24 sigil-ci workflow runs stuck in phase=Running, the oldest since 2026-07-02 (6+ days). Inspecting one (sigil-ci-89lvg) shows its pod is Pending with message: "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient memory, 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector". The sigil-ci-workflowtemplate.yml (jedarden/declarative-config, k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/) requests cpu:2000m/memory:6Gi (limits 4000m/10Gi) per run - the cluster cannot schedule this alongside other workloads, so every sigil-ci run since 07-02 has sat Pending forever (activeDeadlineSeconds:3600 never triggers because it only counts once the pod starts running, not while Pending). Each new push to main (including the low-value "docs: pulse strand false positive" commits) triggers another sensor-fired run that immediately joins the Pending pile.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Reduce sigil-ci-workflowtemplate.yml resource requests/limits to a size the iad-ci cluster can actually schedule (check real node capacity first), OR arrange node capacity - fix lands in jedarden/declarative-config via normal GitOps flow (commit+push, ArgoCD syncs).
2. Clean up the 24+ stuck Pending sigil-ci workflows on iad-ci (they are ArgoCD-unmanaged Argo Workflow CRs, not orphaned pods under a ReplicaSet - deleting stuck Workflow resources is legitimate cleanup, not a declarative-config change).
3. Add a concurrency/dedup limit to the sigil-ci sensor or template (e.g. semaphore or synchronization limiting to 1 concurrent run) so future busywork commits do not pile up duplicate stuck runs.
4. Once unstuck, verify a sigil-ci run actually completes and creates the v0.5.0 GitHub release with all binaries attached (per bf-atfo scope). Confirm via `gh release view v0.5.0 --repo jedarden/SIGIL`.
5. Tag v0.5.0 in git to match the released Cargo.toml version.

The six external SecretBackend implementations (crates/sigil-backend-aws, sigil-backend-onepassword, sigil-backend-sops, sigil-backend-pass, sigil-backend-vault, sigil-backend-env), roughly 4200 lines total of production code implementing get/set/delete/list against real external systems (AWS Secrets Manager, 1Password, SOPS files, pass, HashiCorp Vault, env files), contain zero hash-test-attribute functions in their own src/ directories (grep -c hash-test-attribute across all six crates src files sums to 0).

The only tests referencing these backends live in the sigil-integration-tests crate, in a file named backend underscore integration underscore test dot rs. Inspecting the actual test bodies (for example test_aws_backend_sdk_usage at line 435 and test_aws_backend_rotation_support at line 463) shows they do fs::read_to_string() on the backend crate source file and then assert!(aws_code.contains("version_id")) style substring checks against the raw source text. This never constructs a backend, never calls get/set/delete/list, and never exercises any control flow or error handling - it only confirms certain tokens appear somewhere in the file, which is close to meaningless as a correctness signal and would not catch most real bugs (wrong API usage beyond a missing string, broken error handling, incorrect auth flow, cache invalidation bugs, etc).

The sibling file named external underscore backend underscore e2e underscore test dot rs is more legitimate (constructs real config/router objects and exercises namespace routing, path prefix stripping, serialization) but still never invokes the network-calling get/set/delete/list methods on any backend against a mock server. Notably crates/sigil-backend-vault/Cargo.toml declares mockito = 1.5 as a dev-dependency for exactly this purpose, but there is no test file anywhere in that crate (find crates/sigil-backend-vault -iname *test* returns nothing) - the mocking tool was added but never used.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Add real unit tests inside each of the six backend crates that exercise SecretBackend trait methods against a mock HTTP server (mockito is already a vault dependency; add it or wiremock to the others) covering at minimum: successful get, not-found error, and one auth-failure path.
2. Either delete or rewrite the string-matching tests described above to actually invoke backend behavior instead of grepping source text, or clearly rename or relabel them as documentation checks rather than tests if kept.
3. Note for whoever picks this up: do not add more string-matching source-text assertions as a substitute for behavioral tests - that is the exact anti-pattern this bead exists to fix.

title: FIDO2 hardware-key auth factor is a config-only stub with no actual CTAP/hardware implementation
description:
The plan (Phase 8.6 sealed vault multi-factor unsealing, and the Technology Stack table) specifies ctap-hid-fido2 for "YubiKey integration for hardware-bound unsealing factor" and lists FIDO2 hmac-secret as one of four auth factors (passphrase, device, totp, fido2).

Evidence of what actually exists: crates/sigil-vault/src/config.rs defines `AuthFactorsConfig { passphrase, device, totp, fido2: bool }` with the fido2 flag folded into an auth bitmask (as_bitmask/from_bitmask, bit 0x08). But:
- No crate in the workspace depends on ctap-hid-fido2 or any FIDO2/CTAP/hardware-key library (`grep -rn ctap-hid-fido2 crates/*/Cargo.toml Cargo.toml` = no matches).
- `grep -rn "\.fido2\b" crates/ --include=*.rs` (excluding config.rs and tests) returns zero matches - the flag is never read or acted on anywhere in the unseal/authentication flow.
- No source file anywhere mentions fido2/ctap/Ctap outside crates/sigil-vault/src/config.rs and two integration test files that only check the config struct round-trips (phase8_6_8_7_verification_test.rs, phase8_6_8_7_sealed_vault_redteam_test.rs).

Net effect: a user can set fido2=true in their auth factors config and it will serialize/deserialize and count toward the bitmask, but no hardware key is ever actually challenged or verified - the "factor" contributes nothing to real security. This is misleading for a tool whose entire purpose is protecting secrets.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Either implement real FIDO2 hmac-secret verification (ctap-hid-fido2 or equivalent) wired into the actual unseal/key-derivation path in sigil-vault, matching the Phase 8.6 2SKD design, OR remove the fido2 field/bitmask bit and update plan.md + CHANGELOG to stop claiming FIDO2 support until it exists.
2. If implemented: add a red-team checkpoint test that actually exercises hardware-key-present vs hardware-key-absent unseal attempts (can be behind a hardware-required #[ignore] gate, but must exist).
3. `sigil doctor` should report FIDO2 factor status accurately (currently has no way to know since nothing checks it).

close_reason:
Phase 2.1 daemon hardening verified.

Created comprehensive runtime integration tests that verify all daemon hardening measures are properly implemented:

1. PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 - Confirmed /proc/<pid>/status shows dumpable: 0
2. mlockall(MCL_CURRENT | MCL_FUTURE) - Confirmed memory locking logs
3. Kernel keyring session token - Confirmed token stored in kernel, not file
4. RLIMIT_CORE=0 - Confirmed /proc/<pid>/limits shows core size 0
5. Socket 0600 permissions - Confirmed socket has owner-only permissions

All tests pass.

- **What worked:** The existing daemon implementation already had all the hardening measures in place. The task was primarily verification rather than implementation.

- **Surprise:** The kernel keyring implementation was more complete than expected, including a fallback to file-based storage with proper 0400 permissions for non-Linux systems.
- **Reusable pattern:** Runtime integration tests that spawn a real daemon process and verify /proc filesystem state are an excellent way to validate security hardening that static code analysis cannot confirm.

title: Phase 4: Sandbox Execution Engine — verify and test all providers
description:
sigil-sandbox has bubblewrap, landlock, seatbelt, injection, and state modules (2000+ lines). Need end-to-end testing and verification.

## Key items to verify/complete:

### 4.1 Bubblewrap sandbox
- Full seccomp BPF filter: block ptrace, process_vm_readv/writev, AF_INET/AF_INET6 sockets, mount, io_uring_enter, kexec_load, etc.
- Sensitive path overlays: .env, .aws/credentials, .ssh/*, .gnupg/ → /dev/null
- bwrap --unshare-pid --unshare-net --die-with-parent confirmed working

### 4.2 File injection pipeline
- {{secret:path:file}} → memfd_create(MFD_CLOEXEC) on Linux
- macOS fallback: mkstemp() + immediate unlink()
- tmpfs secret files overwritten with zeros after execution

### 4.3 Shell state tracking
- CWD tracking via :::SIGIL_CWD::: marker
- Exit code via :::SIGIL_EXIT::: marker
- Env var whitelist (block PATH, LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, SHELL changes)

### 4.4 macOS Seatbelt
- SandboxProvider trait with BwrapProvider, SeatbeltProvider, LandlockProvider
- auto-detection logic via is_available()
- PT_DENY_ATTACH for daemon on macOS
- LOCAL_PEERCRED instead of SO_PEERCRED on macOS

### 4.5 TOCTOU mitigations
- pidfd_open() immediately after SO_PEERCRED verification (Linux 5.3+)
- memfd_create for secret injection (no filesystem path to race)
- Fallback for older kernels: /proc/<pid>/exe symlink verification

### 4.6 Full pipeline test
- parse → resolve → sandbox → execute → scrub → return
- Fail loudly if sigild unreachable (no silent passthrough)
- Sandbox overhead < 30ms measured

## Red team checkpoint
- From inside sandbox: attempt /proc/1/environ, ~/.aws/credentials, network, ptrace
- Verify overhead < 30ms with cached secrets
